messages:
Marta (Support): FYI: Several customers reporting function-call failures after the v10.2 canary. Main error: schema validation failed - missing 'payload'. Happening for tool-invokes that worked on v10.1. Repro + logs below. :warning:
Cheng (ML Eng): thx. can you paste raw request/response + request_id + model header?
Marta (Support): pasted from support ticket (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-model-v10.2-canary","input":"...","tools":[{"name":"extractor","args":{"id":"123"}}]}'
```
Response: 400 schema error
```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "validation_error",
    "message": "schema validation failed",
    "details": ["missing required property 'payload'"],
    "request_id": "req_ABC123",
    "model": "redwood-model-v10.2-canary"
  }
}
```
Marta (Support): model header was `x-model: redwood-model-v10.2-canary`. customer says same request worked on v10.1.
Luke (SRE): I'm seeing a spike in canary fleet at 11:03 UTC: higher p50/p95 and token counts. Also traces show double serialization attempts then a validation error on the tool plugin side. log excerpt:
```
[11:03:12] runtime: resolver selected fast-toolpair for tenant=acct_987
[11:03:12] runtime: tool-invoke serialize args -> {"id":"123"} -> after-normalize -> {}
[11:03:12] tool-plugin extractor: validation failed: missing 'payload'
[11:03:12] runtime: fallback attempted -> secondary resolver -> completed with error
```
Cheng (ML Eng): that 'after-normalize -> {}' is the smoking gun. we changed the tool resolver behavior in v10.2 to drop fields considered empty for legacy compatibility. looks like it strips an empty 'payload' object instead of keeping null/empty-object, which breaks strict tool schemas. this wasn't caught in the canary tests because most tests used permissive schemas.
Cheng (ML Eng): quick patch suggestion: rehydrate empty objects before tool-schema validation, or flip the resolver flag to legacy mode.
Marta (Support): also seeing intermittent 403s reported by same customers around same time, and later an unexpected billing spike (customers saw token billing jump). not sure if retries doubled token consumption.
Aisha (Acct Exec): customer is pretty upset and threatening to pause tokens unless we rollback. they want ETA.
Cheng (ML Eng): two options: 1) immediate rollback of canary to v10.1 for affected shards (fastest), 2) push hotfix to rehydrate nulls and deploy to canary (slightly slower). i can prepare hotfix but rollback is safest for customer confidence.
Luke (SRE): i can trigger rollback for the canary group now. will isolate tenants with `fast-toolpair` flag.
OpsBot: Deploy rollback job started -> job_id=rb-4456. Targets: canary pool (shard b, c). Link: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/rb-4456
Luke (SRE): rollback in progress. monitoring p95 and token counts.
Marta (Support): i'll tell customer we've initiated rollback and will follow up as soon as metrics settle. collecting any additional repros. please add any more traces to ticket req_ABC123. :eyes:
Cheng (ML Eng): after rollback, i'll run a small test suite to validate tool-schema preservation and add a unit to prevent stripping empty objects. planning a small config flag default change to avoid regressions.
Luke (SRE): metrics show p95 coming down on rolled-back hosts. billing spike trends also leveling.
Marta (Support): closing the escalation loop with the customer now. will reopen if anything else pops up. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
